claims: The Chicago River is dyed a vibrant emerald green annually for St. Patrick's Day.
The tradition of dyeing the Chicago River for St. Patrick's Day started in 1962.
The dyeing of the Chicago River typically occurs on the Saturday before St. Patrick's Day.
The Chicago Plumbers Union Local 130 uses an eco-friendly, secret vegetable-based dye.
The dye lasts from a few hours up to a couple of days.
The dyeing usually occurs on the Saturday before St. Patrick's Day at 10 a.m.
Plumbers in motorboats pour a secret, orange-powdered dye.
The dye turns bright green upon contact with the water.
The idea for the tradition originated from using dye to trace illegal pollution sources.
The brightest color lasts for several hours.
The dye does not harm fish or wildlife.
CBS News reports the event spans from Wabash Avenue to Lake Shore Drive.
